request.spec:
When I credit part of a surcharged invoice, give back the surcharge on that part too. A credit
note against an invoice with a surcharge carries the same surcharge percentage on what it
credits (rounded down to the cent, and taxed at the same rate as the original's surcharge).
Credit notes still never get a minimum charge.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When I credit part of a surcharged invoice, give back the surcharge on that part too. A credit
note against an invoice with a surcharge carries the same surcharge percentage on what it
credits (rounded down to the cent, and taxed at the same rate as the original's surcharge).
Credit notes still never get a minimum charge.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Credit notes now give back the surcharge on what they credit. `bin/e2e` passes, including the replay of earlier test data. In the test scenario, crediting $50.00 of design work shows a $5.00 surcharge, $0.00 minimum charge and a $59.88 total. The original invoice then shows $59.88 credited and $215.57 due.

What I changed:
- **`Invoice.java`**: a credit note now reads its original invoice's surcharge percentage straight from the database. Nothing new is stored, so no migration or test-data changes were needed. The surcharge is that percentage of what the credit note credits, rounded down to the cent. It is taxed at the same rate as the original's surcharge, which credit notes already used. The minimum charge is still always zero for credit notes.
- **`InvoiceController.java`**: the surcharge percentage sent to the screen is the one actually charged, so a credit note's label reads "Surcharge (10%)" rather than "(0%)".
- **`InvoiceService.java`**: you still can't set a surcharge on a credit note yourself. I only reworded the error message to say that it carries the surcharge of the invoice it credits.

The credit note always uses the original's surcharge percentage as it is right now, not a copy taken when the credit note was created. In practice that shouldn't differ, because the surcharge can only be changed on a draft and only sent invoices can be credited.
